title: Price shock probabilistic HC decision tree
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, actionable decision tree that maps price/revenue shock outcomes to headcount (HC) and budget multiplier actions for FY27 planning. This is a probabilistic, trigger-based playbook intended to supplement the Q4 budget cadence and the dedicated capacity hiring plan. Not a final approval artifact — use for scenario planning and SLT discussion.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We model 3 price-shock buckets (Mild, Moderate, Severe) with assigned probabilities based on market pulse and sales funnel (see assumptions).
- Each bucket has recommended budget multipliers (applied to non-headline OPEX categories) and HC actions (freeze, pause, selective hiring).
- Expected value (EV) approach produces an incremental HC staging policy that preserves critical SRE/Infra and product-roadmap hires while delaying lower-priority roles.
- Triggers are explicit KPI thresholds (7-day bookings delta, committed ARR conversion, tokens/route churn) so the response can be automated where possible.

Key assumptions (inputs to the model):
- Baseline FY27 ARR cadence assumes 35% YoY growth in hosted API ARR absent shocks.
- Price shock definition = realized average effective price per 1k tokens across top 200 customers vs. baseline.
- Mild shock = -8% price; Moderate = -20%; Severe = -40% (severity calibrated to competitor discounting and channel pressure scenarios).
- Probability (subjective prior for planning): Mild 50%, Moderate 35%, Severe 15% (sensitivity later shows wide variance).
- Critical hires protected: SRE lead (2 FTEs), infra HW ops (3 FTEs), model-migration engineers (2 FTEs) — these are not reduced in Mild or Moderate, only reviewed in Severe.

Model overview (how to read the decision tree):
- Node A: Observe rolling 30-day effective price change (booking-weighted). If delta > -8%, stay in baseline hiring plan.
- Node B (Mild): If delta between -8% and -20% for 14 consecutive days AND booking pipeline conversion drop > 10%, apply mild mitigations.
- Node C (Moderate): If delta between -20% and -40% OR churn among top 50 customers increases > 5ppts, apply moderate mitigations and start 60-day hiring pause for non-essential roles.
- Node D (Severe): If delta <= -40% or committed ARR loss > 10% quarter-to-date, escalate to exec review and implement aggressive multipliers and targeted layoffs if necessary.

Recommended budget multipliers by shock bucket (apply to non-headline OPEX categories: marketing, travel, third-party services):
- Baseline: multiplier 1.0 (no change)
- Mild: multiplier 0.88 (12% cut) — focus: pause non-critical marketing campaigns, pause vendor onboarding with >6w ramp, reduce conference spend by 80%
- Moderate: multiplier 0.70 (30% cut) — pause most marketing, freeze contractor renewals, renegotiate vendor SLAs for volume discounts, defer data retention expansion
- Severe: multiplier 0.45 (55% cut) — all discretionary spend halted, preserve top-customer SLA spend and security/compliance spend only

Headcount phasing (recommended actions by role priority):
- Protected pool (no change unless Severe): SRE (2), Infra-HW (3), Model infra (2), Security (2)
- Priority hires (evaluate for selective continuation under Mild): Core infra engineers, Dedicated sales reps for top accounts, Account success for largest 30 customers
- Flexible hires (immediate pause under Moderate): Marketing demand gen, early-stage partnerships, non-critical product research, campus/new-grad roles
- Back-office (gradual reduction under Moderate/Severe): Non-essential contractors, open reqs in ops/people team (freeze in Moderate)

Incremental HC decision table (examples, show EV logic in prose):
- Baseline plan: +24 net FTEs across FY27 (staged monthly).
- Under Mild (EV-adjusted): de-risk by shifting 40% of planned hires from Q1–Q2 into Q3–Q4 (net realized +14 by EOY if shock persists).
- Under Moderate: immediate 60-day hiring pause for flexible hires; realize +8 net FTEs by EOY (reallocations and slower ramp).
- Under Severe: convert to a prioritized reduction to preserve runway: cancel 100% of flexible hires, evaluate up to 8 FTE reductions in non-customer-facing teams (final subject to exec sign-off).

Trigger thresholds (operational KPIs to monitor daily/weekly):
- Effective price per 1k tokens (booking-weighted): trigger Mild at -8% sustained 14d; Moderate -20% sustained 10d; Severe -40% sustained 5d
- Top-50 customer churn (MoM): +3ppts triggers Moderate review, +5ppts triggers Severe review
- New committed ARR conversion rate (funnel): drop >12% vs baseline triggers Moderate
- Dedicated capacity commitments: loss of >2 committed customers with >$50k MRR triggers Immediate exec notification

Sensitivity & backtest notes:
- Running Monte Carlo with a 30% stddev on price-change input moves Severe probability between 5%–25% — highest sensitivity to sales pipeline health and competitor public pricing.
- In earlier drafts we assumed higher protection for marketing spend; backtests show marketing cut elasticity is lower (i.e., cutting marketing reduces bookings by ~0.4x of spend reduction) — hence the asymmetry in multipliers.

Operational play & messaging:
- If Mild triggers: Finance issues a 14-day notice to recruiting + hiring managers to shift timelines; procurement pauses non-critical purchases automatically via PO hold; CFO sends a short note to SLT with status and next checkpoint date.
- If Moderate: recruiting freeze enacted, contractors on 30-day notice where possible; Customer Success is prioritized for outreach to top-50 customers with assigned AE owners.
- If Severe: convene exec response team (CFO/CEO/Head of Sales/Head of Eng/SVP People) with a 48-hour action window. Layoff plan templates pre-approved but not executed until exec sign-off.

Open questions / decision points for SLT:
- Do we accept the baseline prior probabilities (50/35/15) or substitute market-informed priors from Sales Ops (need inputs by Nov 16)?
- Which hiring reqs are reclassified as "protected" vs "priority" — require cross-functional alignment from Eng/Product/CS by Nov 20.
- Approve automated procurement PO holds for mild triggers?

Next steps (owner + dates):
- Sales Ops to provide funnel-based priors by 2026-11-16 (Owner: Marcus Chen)
- People Ops to mark open reqs with priority tags and maturity (Owner: Priya Desai) by 2026-11-20
- Finance to wire the budget multipliers into the Q4 budgeting sheet and run EV scenarios (Owner: Sophie Lin) by 2026-11-17

Appendix (quick math examples):
- Example: Baseline planned spend for marketing FY27 = $8.5M. Under Moderate multiplier (0.70) -> adjusted spend = $5.95M, delta = $2.55M saving. That covers ~6 FTE equivalent fully-loaded cost at current hiring mix.
- Example: If Mild persists 3 months and then reverts to baseline, the EV-adjusted net hires realized shrinks by ~40% due to staged reprioritization and delayed start dates.
